newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa slips in thin volume on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa slips in thin volume on liquidation.

text.p: A weak round of long liquidation sent London cocoa futures lower on Monday but there was no news to bite on, traders said.
"I expect nothing much will happen until after Christmas," said one.
"All last week was currency and some speculative elements but now that's finished trade houses are liquidating their longs," he added.
Earlier traders linked sales with disappointment over the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders Report which showed that New York might have exhausted its potential for speculative short covering.
The data for two weeks ending December 3 showed speculators moved to a net long of 6,000 lots after buying back 9,000 lots.

At the close of business, the benchmark March position had shed 12 stg a tonne to 934, backing further away from nearby resistance of 950. The lowest for the day was 930. Other contracts lost up to 14 stg.
Turnover was a meagre 2,700 lots which included switches with March/May trading at 20 stg.
Technically, the market remained above the key support level of 927 stg on March, still holding the potential for a foray into the 950-960 area.
Elsewhere in Ghana, populist president Jerry Rawlings was heading for victory with almost half the results of Saturday's presidential and parliamentary elections gathered.

No fresh word emerged on West African crops after last week's forecasts which puzzled traders with a wide range of estimates. Analysts say new arrival figures until the end of January should trim the margin for error which is considered to be around 35 percent now.
